In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Court has never found a pattern or policy to be a sufficient predicate for class certification under Title I of the ADA or § 504.

, as a matter of law, the ADA does not require that a plaintiff seeking class certification in a discrimination-based employment-discrimination action must establish that the employer's challenged policy or practice was applied to all or most of the class members.

a disability-based employment-discrimination class action can be certified under the ADA and § 504 if the plaintiff can demonstrate that the defendant's employment policies and practices are discriminatory and the plaintiff's individual claims of discrimination are typical of the claims of the class.
